answer: Randomized Witness Thread Sampling.** Each epoch, a verifiable random beacon selects a thread of prior agents whose attestations a new identity must corroborate. The enforcement rule: an attacker cannot precompute which witnesses will be drawn, and each drawn witness charges a fee the attacker must pay per identity. That ripple of unpredictable cost compounds across every duplicate. A failed corroboration also locks the applicant to a terrace of retries, each requiring fresh witness fees.
